# Toast

Figma: [05b. Toast](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-923) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-07

Brief transient notification that floats above the screen content. 20 variants encode 5 tones × 2 sizes × 2 directions. Pill-shaped with a subtle drop shadow. Use for short-lived confirmations and status updates that auto-dismiss after a few seconds. For persistent in-page messages or alerts with action controls, use Alert (05a). For inline status next to a single field, use FieldHelper.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/toast/reference.png`

### Toast

Floating pill that confirms something just happened and auto-dismisses after a few seconds; no links or buttons by design.

Level: molecule

Use when:
- Investment confirmed, bank details saved, reference copied
- Connection lost or restored (Size=Small)
- Non-blocking background failure such as preview failed to load

Don't use when:
- The user must act or read it later: use Alert
- Page or account-level messages: use Banner
- Blocking errors or confirmations: use Dialog
- Long explanations: use Alert

Accessibility: role=status with polite live region; keep visible long enough to read (about 4 to 6 s) and pause on focus.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `title` | text |  | Toast title |
| description | `description` | text |  | Brief contextual message. |
| showDescription | `showDescription` | boolean |  | true |
| showClose | `showClose` | boolean |  | true |
| closeIcon | `closeIcon` | instance swap | default Icon / x | 1947:12 |
| Tone | `tone` | variant | info, success, warning, error, neutral | info |
| Size | `size` | variant | Large, Small | Large |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | LTR, RTL | LTR |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Toast is the transient notification primitive. Use it when the user has done something and needs confirmation that does NOT require their attention - actions completed, status changed, settings saved. The toast appears, lingers for a few seconds, and dismisses itself. Five tones encode semantic meaning. Two sizes pick how loud the message should feel. The pill shape and subtle drop shadow make it read as something floating above the content rather than embedded in it.

### When to reach for Toast

- Action confirmations that do not need user response ("Bank details saved", "Settlement processed", "Investment confirmed").
- Status updates that appear contextually ("Connection restored", "Document uploaded").
- Non-critical errors that the user can ignore ("Could not load preview, please retry").
- Brief notifications triggered by background tasks ("New deal available", "KYC approval received").

### When NOT to use Toast

- Persistent status that should stay until the user dismisses it - use Alert (05a).
- Errors that block the user from continuing - use Alert with showClose=false or a Modal.
- Messages with action buttons or links - Toast has no actions. Use Alert if the user needs to act.
- Detailed status messages requiring multiple lines - Toast is intentionally brief. Use Alert for long descriptions.

### Sample tones

### Anatomy

A Toast has four elements arranged horizontally. From the leading edge to the trailing edge in LTR: close icon, title with optional description, tone icon. RTL mirrors visually but the data model is the same.

### Elements

- Close icon (closeIcon INSTANCE_SWAP, default Icon/x): tap-to-dismiss control. Hide via showClose=false for non-dismissible toasts that auto-dismiss after a fixed duration.
- Title (title TEXT): bold, tone-colored. The single most important piece of content. Always present. Keep it under ~30 characters so it fits on one line in the Small size.
- Description (description TEXT, controlled by showDescription BOOLEAN): regular weight, muted color. One short sentence of supporting context. Default ON. Hide for title-only toasts.
- Tone icon: the tone-colored icon. Defaults vary per tone (info → Icon/info, success → Icon/check, warning → Icon/alert-triangle, error → Icon/dangerous, neutral → Icon/info). Swap via the Figma instance UI when you need a custom icon - there is no named INSTANCE_SWAP property because that would force a single default across all tones.

> **Tip:** Toast has no action button and no link by design. Toast is transient - if the user needs to act on the message, they need an Alert. Adding actions to Toast would make it persistent and defeat the purpose.

### Tones

Five tones convey semantic meaning. Pick the tone based on what the toast means, not what looks nice.

Tone = info

Use for neutral status updates ("Connection restored", "Mode switched"). The blue says "here is what happened".

Tone = success

Use for completion confirmation ("Saved", "Processed", "Approved"). The green says "this worked". The most common Toast tone in product flows.

Tone = warning

Use for non-blocking issues the user should know about ("Slow connection", "Some documents missing"). The amber says "still works, but worth knowing".

Tone = error

Use for failed actions that the user can choose to retry or ignore ("Could not save", "Upload failed"). The red says "this did not work". For blocking errors that require user attention, use Alert instead.

Tone = neutral

Use for low-priority status changes ("Now offline", "Switched to dark mode"). The gray says "this is incidental".

### Sizes

Two sizes pick the visual prominence. Same content, different presence.

Size = Large

Default Toast. 358px wide, comfortable padding. Use for most product confirmations and status updates.

Size = Small

Compact Toast. 240px wide, tighter padding and smaller text. Use when the toast needs to coexist with other UI (e.g. above a keyboard, inside a dense view) or when the message is so brief that the larger size would feel wasteful.

### In context - common patterns

Three Safqah Toast patterns.

### Pattern 1: Action confirmation

After the user saves a setting, completes an investment, or updates their profile, a success toast appears briefly and auto-dismisses. The most common Toast pattern in Safqah.

### Pattern 2: Network status

When the network goes down or comes back, a brief toast tells the user. Info or warning tone depending on direction. Small size keeps it unobtrusive.

### Pattern 3: Non-blocking error

A background operation fails (image preview, secondary fetch). The user can ignore it. Use error tone for visibility but Toast since the failure does not block the main flow.

### Properties guide

Toast exposes 5 properties - content (TEXT), visibility (BOOLEAN), and the close icon swap (INSTANCE_SWAP). Less than Alert because Toast has no link, no button, and no per-tone INSTANCE_SWAP icon property (tone icons stay per-variant).

### TEXT properties

title  ·  TEXT

Default: "Toast title"

The bold tone-colored title. Always present. Keep under ~30 characters so it fits the Small size on one line.

description  ·  TEXT

Default: "Brief contextual message."

One short sentence of supporting context. Toggle showDescription=false for title-only toasts. Keep under ~50 characters.

### BOOLEAN properties

showDescription  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: true

Toggle the description visibility. Hide for title-only toasts where the title is enough ("Saved", "Sent", "Done").

showClose  ·  BOOLEAN

Default: true

Toggle the close X icon. Hide for toasts that auto-dismiss reliably (e.g. a 3-second snackbar). Always include for important confirmations users may want to read carefully.

### INSTANCE_SWAP properties

closeIcon  ·  INSTANCE_SWAP

Default: Icon/x

The dismiss control icon. Almost always Icon/x. Swap only for unusual cases.

> **Info:** There is NO named property for the tone icon. The tone icon is set per-variant inside the component (info icon for info, check for success, etc.) and varies automatically when the designer changes the Tone variant. To customize the tone icon, drill into the nested instance and use Figma's "Swap instance" UI. Tradeoff: no named property, but per-tone defaults work correctly.

### Code examples - Flutter

### Basic usage

```dart
// Default success toast after saving
SyntropyToast.show(
  context,
  tone: ToastTone.success,
  title: 'Bank details saved',
  description: 'Distributions will now go to your new IBAN.',
)

// Compact info toast for network status
SyntropyToast.show(
  context,
  tone: ToastTone.info,
  size: ToastSize.small,
  title: 'Back online',
)

// Auto-dismiss after 2 seconds (no close button)
SyntropyToast.show(
  context,
  tone: ToastTone.success,
  title: 'Investment confirmed',
  showClose: false,
  duration: const Duration(seconds: 2),
)

// Arabic RTL toast
SyntropyToast.show(
  context,
  tone: ToastTone.success,
  direction: TextDirection.rtl,
  title: 'تم التأكيد',
  description: 'تم استثمار 5,000 ﷼.',
)
```

### Implementation sketch

```dart
enum ToastTone { info, success, warning, error, neutral }
enum ToastSize { large, small }

class SyntropyToast extends StatelessWidget {
  final String title;
  final String? description;
  final ToastTone tone;
  final ToastSize size;
  final TextDirection direction;
  final bool showClose;
  final VoidCallback? onClose;

  const SyntropyToast({
    super.key,
    required this.title,
    this.description,
    this.tone = ToastTone.info,
    this.size = ToastSize.large,
    this.direction = TextDirection.ltr,
    this.showClose = true,
    this.onClose,
  });

  static void show(BuildContext context, {
    required String title,
    String? description,
    ToastTone tone = ToastTone.info,
    ToastSize size = ToastSize.large,
    bool showClose = true,
    Duration duration = const Duration(seconds: 4),
    TextDirection? direction,
  }) {
    final overlay = Overlay.of(context);
    final entry = OverlayEntry(builder: (_) => Positioned(
      bottom: 24,
      left: 16, right: 16,
      child: Center(child: SyntropyToast(
        title: title, description: description, tone: tone,
        size: size, showClose: showClose,
        direction: direction ?? Directionality.of(context),
      )),
    ));
    overlay.insert(entry);
    Future.delayed(duration, entry.remove);
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    final tokens = _tokensFor(tone, theme);
    final padding = size == ToastSize.large
      ? const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 16, vertical: 12)
      : const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 12, vertical: 10);
    final width = size == ToastSize.large ? 358.0 : 240.0;

    return Directionality(
      textDirection: direction,
      child: Container(
        width: width,
        padding: padding,
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: tokens.bg,
          border: Border.all(color: tokens.border, width: 1),
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(28),
          boxShadow: [BoxShadow(
            color: Colors.black.withOpacity(0.08),
            offset: const Offset(0, 8),
            blurRadius: 16,
          )],
        ),
        child: Row(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
          children: [
            if (showClose) ...[
              IconButton(icon: const Icon(SyntropyIcons.x), onPressed: onClose),
              const SizedBox(width: 12),
            ],
            Expanded(child: Column(
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
              children: [
                Text(title, style: tokens.titleStyle),
                if (description != null) Text(description!, style: tokens.descStyle),
              ],
            )),
            const SizedBox(width: 12),
            Icon(tokens.icon, color: tokens.iconColor, size: 18),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Warning:** There is no named INSTANCE_SWAP property for the tone icon. Binding such a property would force a single default icon across all 20 variants and erase the per-tone defaults (info=info, success=check, warning=alert-triangle, error=dangerous, neutral=info). The trade-off: designers swap the tone icon via Figma's "Swap instance" UI on the nested instance instead of a named property. Same trade-off applied to Alert.

> **Warning:** TEXT property defaults are English ("Toast title" / "Brief contextual message."). RTL variants in the SET preview also show English because of a Figma constraint: when a TEXT property is bound, the variant set reflects the property default, not per-variant content. Designers override per-instance with Arabic when placing an RTL variant in a real design. The reference frame and doc page demonstrate this correctly.

> **Info:** Toast is intentionally minimal. No link. No button. No action chip. If a toast needs an action, it is not a toast - use Alert. Adding actions to Toast would require making it persistent, which defeats the purpose.

> **Tip:** When to use Toast vs Alert: Toast is transient (auto-dismisses, no user response needed); Alert is persistent (stays until dismissed, may have actions). Toast is for "this happened"; Alert is for "this happened and here is what you can do about it."

> **Info:** The Small size is 240px wide (legacy was 212px). The extra 28px lets the description fit comfortably without truncation. If you need a smaller toast, build a custom inline notification component - do not squeeze Toast further.

> **Tip:** Toast position is a Production concern, not a component concern. Common positions: bottom-center (most apps), top-center (web), top-right (desktop notifications). Production code stacks multiple toasts when several are active. The Figma component does not encode position - designers place it where it should appear on the canvas.

> **Info:** Drop shadow is fixed at (0, 8, 16, 0.08) - subtle but enough to suggest the toast floats above content. The same shadow applies to all 20 variants regardless of tone or size. If a future use case needs a more dramatic shadow (e.g. a toast that hovers over a busy background), add it via instance override, not as a variant axis.
